posts.title: Elk rut season: how not to get charged

slides.headline: It's elk rut season. Give them room.
Ears back = back off.
details: If an elk gets alert or nervous, grinds its teeth or puts its ears back, you're too close.
Never get between a bull and the females. Not on foot, not in your car.

slides.headline: Do not play dead.
details: Make yourself big: raise your arms, a jacket or an umbrella. Keep eye contact. Never turn your back or run.
Get a tree or a big rock between you and the elk, then back slowly away.

slides.headline: Leash the dog.
details: Elk see an off-leash dog as a wolf or coyote.
Report any elk incident to Banff Dispatch: 403-762-1470.

posts.caption:
ELK RUT SEASON 🦌 The bulls are fired up, and Parks Canada wants you to give them room.

• Stay at least 30 metres back. That's about 3 bus lengths.
• Ears back or teeth grinding? You're too close. Back off.
• Never get between a bull and the females, and don't park there either.
• If one charges: make yourself big, keep eye contact, don't run. Do not play dead.
• Keep your dog on a leash.

Incidents in Banff: Banff Dispatch 403-762-1470.

Send this to whoever's driving to the mountains this weekend.

Source: Parks Canada (Banff elk safety and elk rut advisory). Photo: Jakub Fryš, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons.
